solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What's expected of orchestra, pure playing

indicators.note: the orchestra playing suggests these letters being worked through and rearranged

explanation.surface: An orchestra playing pure music is just what an audience expects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges OF ORCHESTRA PURE; the 'of' belongs to the fodder, not just to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the normal, predictable outcome, as a golf score of par is the standard for a hole.

clue.text: Birds wanting home when caught in air currents

indicators.note: one piece is caught inside another, so the word for home sits within the currents

parts.note: puffs are small gusts of air
in means at home

explanation.surface: Birds are blown off course by gusts, longing for their nests.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffins are seabirds with bright striped beaks.

clue.text: Stir created by French author's introduction being cut

indicators.note: the opening letter of the writer's name is cut away

parts.note: Marcel Proust was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A literary scandal: trimming a French author's preface caused a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse or stir someone out of bed or into action.

clue.text: Possible clue to mad don being a misfit

parts.note: read as wordplay, the letters O D D M A N worked 'out' (rearranged) give MAD DON, so the phrase could clue those words

explanation.surface: A puzzling clue about an eccentric academic who does not fit in.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'odd' and 'out' both act as anagram signals on MAN and ODD, and the result is the phrase mad don.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the one person who does not belong in a group, a misfit.

clue.text: Tease silly person

definitions.meaning: to taunt or mock someone gently
a fool or idiot, in informal British use

explanation.surface: Mock a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is an old word for teasing; the noun is slang for a foolish person.

clue.text: Get weight reduced somehow — one component of breakfast food?

indicators.note: done somehow means in some rearranged order of letters
the word weight is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A dieter tries to lose weight by eating only part of the breakfast plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' trims WEIGHT to WEIGH; 'somehow' rearranges GET plus WEIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg, a breakfast staple, consists of yolk and albumen, the clear part that sets white when cooked.

clue.text: Old invalid like Humpty Dumpty

parts.note: a void contract is invalid, of no legal force

explanation.surface: An elderly sick person resembles the nursery-rhyme character who fell off a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' looks like a sick person but means not legally binding.
explanation.definitionFit: Humpty Dumpty is drawn as an egg, and egg-shaped is the literal sense.

clue.text: Like a memory of event — tries forgetting the end somehow

indicators.note: done somehow means the letters can come in any rearranged order
the final letter of tries is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone tries to recall an event but forgets how it finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting the end' trims TRIES to TRIE; 'somehow' rearranges EVENT plus TRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A good memory holds on to things; retentive describes that capacity to keep information.

clue.text: Energy and most of remaining protein

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: everything except the final letter is kept

parts.note: lasting means enduring or remaining

explanation.surface: A sports drink promises energy and lasting protein.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a stretchy connective-tissue protein found in skin and arteries.

clue.text: Neglected child needs caressing, housing of superior character

indicators.note: one word holds another within it

parts.note: fondling means stroking tenderly
U is the letter for upper-class, superior, usage in British English

explanation.surface: An abandoned child longs for affection and a home with good values.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant abandoned by its parents and found by others, so a neglected child.

clue.text: Seaman comes to island, back in old harbour

parts.note: OS is ordinary seaman

indicators.note: the word for island is read from end to start

parts.note: an ait or eyot is a small river island

explanation.surface: A sailor returns to an island and its ancient port.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the port of ancient Rome at the Tiber's mouth.

clue.text: I beam, receiving collection of books — something to put on desk

indicators.note: the outer letters take the inner piece into them

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone beams with pride over a set of books on the desk.
explanation.definitionFit: An office tray holding incoming letters and paperwork waiting to be dealt with.

clue.text: TV doctor had one work of fiction

parts.note: Doctor Who is the long-running BBC science-fiction series
having had a go is having 'done it', spelt the slangy way 'dun it'

explanation.surface: A TV doctor wrote a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The genre name is itself slang for 'who done it?', the question a detective story poses.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective novel or play built around identifying the murderer.

clue.text: Would-be lover wanting men at back of clubs?

indicators.note: the men come after the clubs in the answer

parts.note: clubs is one suit in a deck of cards
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A lonely-hearts figure wants men from the back of the nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A man courting a woman is her prospective partner or admirer.

clue.text: Prisoners put down, observed to be upset

parts.note: to inter is to bury, put down in the ground

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: seen means observed

explanation.surface: Prisoners are upset at being put down and watched.
explanation.definitionFit: People held in confinement, typically in wartime, without trial.

clue.text: Horse above average height, one reined in by boy

indicators.note: held in as a rider restrains a horse, so inside

parts.note: a son is a boy
tall means above average height
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tall horse is held back by a young rider.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse, especially one kept for breeding.

clue.text: Freedom, with saints for the first time showing sluggishness

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out at its first appearance only

parts.note: latitude means scope or freedom of action

explanation.surface: Free for the first time, the saints appear lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first T of LATITUDE changes; the second stays.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is weariness or lethargy, a lack of energy.

clue.text: Foreign lady in trick, valuable person going the wrong way

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick

indicators.note: travelling in reverse, so read backwards

parts.note: an asset is a useful or valuable person

explanation.surface: A foreign noblewoman is caught up in a swindle when an associate goes astray.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian countess, a title for a foreign noblewoman.

clue.text: A bit that's positive about Italian in honourable mention

indicators.note: going around another piece

parts.note: a cation is a positively charged ion, a tiny bit of matter

explanation.surface: A positive word about an Italian earns a commendation.
explanation.definitionFit: A citation is a formal commendation, for example for bravery in military dispatches.

clue.text: Restricted in temporary accommodation to house refugees primarily

indicators.note: giving shelter to, so placing inside

parts.note: camped means living in tents or temporary lodgings

indicators.note: the first letter of refugees is taken

explanation.surface: Refugees are confined in a camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Cramped means confined or short of space, so restricted.

clue.text: Consider hunt gatherings savage ultimately, on reflection

indicators.note: as in a mirror, the letters are read backwards

parts.note: meets are gatherings of a fox hunt before riding out

indicators.note: the final letter of savage is used

explanation.surface: Someone reflects that fox-hunting meets are ultimately savage.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem can mean to regard or deem, as in 'I esteem it an honour'.

clue.text: Most intimate relations shown in a bit of coarse material

indicators.note: displayed within another word

parts.note: a mat is a piece of coarse woven fabric
ties are bonds or relations

explanation.surface: Close relationships are depicted on a scrap of rough fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Matey means friendly and familiar, and the superlative is the friendliest.

clue.text: Claim spa town is lacking hospital

indicators.note: missing a letter, so it is removed

parts.note: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire, England
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Residents claim their spa town has no hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to seize or lay claim to something without right.

clue.text: Pick up from valley around start of autumn

indicators.note: the valley word goes round the other letter

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland

indicators.note: the first letter of autumn

explanation.surface: Collect things from a valley as autumn begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather leftover grain, or to pick up information bit by bit.

clue.text: Rocky location with risk — one approaching it may be doomed

definitions.text: one approaching it may be doomed

parts.note: Gib is short for Gibraltar, the Rock
a bet is a risk or wager

explanation.surface: A rocky place where taking chances could be fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: A condemned person walks up to the gallows-like post from which executed bodies hung.

clue.text: Indifferent and mean, having trapped girl finally

indicators.note: holding something caught inside

parts.note: base means low or mean in character

indicators.note: finally means at the very end, so only the closing letter of girl is used

explanation.surface: Someone cold and nasty has ensnared a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Unimpressed and unconcerned through over-familiarity, so indifferent.

clue.text: One of the players in the side

definitions.meaning: a winger, a team member positioned on the flank in rugby or hockey
a flank, or a side part of a building or stage

explanation.surface: A member of the team.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a flank player and a lateral part of a building or army.

clue.text: Part of City invested in Indian money no longer

indicators.note: put into, as money is invested, so inside

parts.note: the pie was a small Indian coin, no longer used
EC is the postal district of the City of London

explanation.surface: Part of the City's money was put into an obsolete Indian currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or bit of a whole.

clue.text: Insist on fan keeping quiet for minutes

indicators.note: retaining something in place of a letter
one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: to fan the flames is to stimulate them
P, piano, is the music direction for quiet

explanation.surface: An enthusiast insists on silence during the minutes of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipulate is to demand or specify something as a condition.

clue.text: Release from complicated relationship — gentleman ends it with difficulty

indicators.note: achieved with effort and struggle, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: A man ends a messy affair, not without struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: Extricating oneself from a tangle or an involvement is freeing oneself.
